notes: UNION ALL of a customer-transactions arm and a supplier-transactions arm, each windowed on LastEditedWhen (@LastCutoff, @NewCutoff]. Customer arm: CT 1 (2020-01-20) has an InvoiceID -> LEFT JOIN Invoices hits -> COALESCE picks i.CustomerID; CT 2 (2020-02-20) has NULL InvoiceID -> COALESCE falls back to ct.CustomerID. Supplier arm: ST 1 (2020-01-20). This proc has NO final ORDER BY, so row order is not guaranteed -- captured with ordered=false (canonicaliser sorts by row value) so the golden is stable across re-captures regardless of plan. It is the one tranche-1 proc where the ORDER BY mutation has nothing to break, by the proc's own design.

cases.name: jan-both-arms
cases.why: Jan window returns CT 1 (customer arm, COALESCE i-side) AND ST 1 (supplier arm) -> the UNION ALL emits both arms in one result. Supplier arm carries SupplierInvoiceNumber; customer arm has it null.

cases.name: feb-coalesce-fallback
cases.why: Feb window returns CT 2 only (customer arm): NULL InvoiceID -> COALESCE(i.CustomerID, ct.CustomerID) falls back to ct.CustomerID. No supplier row in Feb.

cases.name: both-months
cases.why: Wide window returns CT 1, CT 2 and ST 1 -> both customer COALESCE branches and the supplier arm together.

cases.name: empty-window
cases.why: Window before any edit -> empty (both arms yield nothing).
